Prefer fixed, cloned diagnostic batches captured from batches training already consumes, or generated through a separate dataset/loader with independent RNGs. Do not populate the cache by advancing the training iterator. This recommendation follows from DataLoader behavior: iterator creation consumes RNG for worker seeds; prefetching advances sampling beyond returned batches; persistent workers retain dataset instances and evolving worker state. Restoring parent RNGs cannot rewind worker RNGs, queues, dataset mutations or custom sampler cursors. [DataLoader documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html)

RNG restoration is sufficient only when all affected state is controlled. Snapshot Python, NumPy, default Torch CPU and relevant CUDA RNG states, plus every dedicated generator used by loaders, samplers and transforms; restore custom sampler/dataset state separately. `torch.random.fork_rng` covers default CPU/device RNGs, not arbitrary generators or worker processes. For multiprocessing or persistent workers, cached batches or an isolated diagnostic loader provide a stronger practical guarantee than attempting to rewind the training loader. Cache tensors independently and prevent probes from modifying them. [Torch RNG documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html), [reproducibility guidance](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/randomness.md)

For model execution, record each submodule’s training flag, enter evaluation mode, and use `no_grad()` or `inference_mode()`; gradient suppression alone does not disable dropout or buffer updates. Restore individual flags to preserve mixed modes. Audit custom forwards and existing hooks for mutations; protect mutable buffers, including nonpersistent buffers, and other custom state. Avoid backward calls and optimizer updates. Use `try/finally` to remove every diagnostic hook, restore protected state and RNGs, and release references even after exceptions. Ordinary `state_dict()` snapshots omit nonpersistent buffers and require cloning to avoid aliasing. [Module documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.Module.html), [inference-mode documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html)
